topic: The 10 free Claude skills in the AI Every Time starter kit
audience: Professionals who use Claude every day but paste the same instructions again and again
goal: Download the starter kit and install one skill today
notes: A skill is a small folder of instructions (sometimes scripts and templates) that teaches Claude one job the way you want it done. Install it once; Claude picks it up whenever a request needs it.
Every skill has one required file, SKILL.md. Its name is also the command you can type, such as /learn-anything; its description says what it does and when to use it.
Skills load in layers: always just the name and description; the instructions when a request matches; extra files only if needed. So you can install many without slowing Claude down.

The ten skills (written by Mojeed for AI Every Time learners): learn-anything (teaches any topic step by step from what you already know), quiz-me (turns notes into practice questions, one at a time), research-brief (a short sourced brief with a confidence level for each finding), news-explainer (what happened, why it matters, who it affects), job-application (tailors a CV and cover letter to a specific job ad, honestly), linkedin-post (posts in your own voice), meeting-to-actions (decisions, actions with owners and deadlines, follow-up email), presentation-planner (one message per slide, speaker notes), check-the-numbers (profiles the file and proves the answer first), skill-maker (drafts, checks and zips your own skill).

Install: 1) download the zip, don't unzip it; 2) Settings → Capabilities → turn on 'Create and edit files' (older layout: 'Code execution and file creation'); 3) Customize → Skills → + → Create skill → Upload a skill; 4) check the switch is on.
Every skill in the library is plain text you can read in a minute; read every file before you switch a skill on.
The guide also has a library of 120 more skills for 20 jobs.

Rules for making a skill: name in lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, 64 characters at most; description says what it does and when to use it, 200 characters at most in the Claude apps; instructions under 500 lines. Test with 3 requests that should use it and 2 that shouldn't; if Claude misses one, improve the description first.

Claude Code: unzip into ~/.claude/skills/ for every project, or a project's .claude/skills/ folder (commit it); /skills lists what's installed. Team plans: skills on by default; Enterprise: an owner turns them on first.
